newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Momentum says pulp prices could rise.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Momentum says pulp prices could rise.

text.p: Swedish pulp and paper consultancy firm Momentum said on Friday a raise in pulp prices might be in the cards in late spring.

A strong order intake on fine paper, expected production halts at pulp mills and a slightly lower than expected increase of North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks speak in favour of higher prices, Momentum said.
"Personally I had feared a larger increase in pulp stocks considering all pulp mills are running at full capacity," Momentum spokesman Bernt Stenberg told Reuters.
"It will be necessary with several production halts during the spring as mills have been working at high capacity for a long time, and then stocks will decrease quickly."
NorScan pulp stocks rose by 70,000 tonnes in February from January to more than 2.1 million tonnes, according to non-traded Swedish forestry group Sodra Skogsagarna.
The stocks were thereby 400,000 tonnes lower than they were a year ago. At this time last year, prices started to fall, which normally is the case, Stenberg said.
"And when stocks come down to about 1.6-1.7 million tonnes a price increase is possible," Stenberg said.
Stenberg also predicted a strong order intake on fine paper.
"Demand for fine paper is currently high," he said.
On the negative side he noted that a great deal of capacity had been added since then.
